spec: Build a URL shortener API. Clients submit a long URL and receive a short code; visiting the short code redirects to the original URL and increments a visit counter. Include an endpoint returning the visit statistics for a code. Mappings are stored in DynamoDB.

plan.summary: A URL shortener API where clients submit a long URL to receive a short code, visiting the short code redirects to the original URL and increments a visit counter, and statistics for a code can be retrieved. Mappings are persisted in DynamoDB.

endpoints.purpose: Accept a long URL and return a generated short code with its short URL.
Redirect to the original long URL and increment the visit counter for the code.
Return visit statistics (visit count, original URL, creation time) for a given short code.

aws_resources.name: url_mappings
aws_resources.justification: Stores the short code to long URL mappings and the visit counter, as required by the spec.

aws_resources.name: url_shortener_fn
aws_resources.justification: Runs the FastAPI application handling shorten, redirect, and stats endpoints.

aws_resources.name: url_shortener_api
aws_resources.justification: Exposes the Lambda-backed HTTP endpoints to external clients.

aws_resources.name: url_shortener_lambda_role
aws_resources.justification: Grants the Lambda function permission to read/write the DynamoDB table and write logs.

aws_resources.name: url_shortener_logs
aws_resources.justification: Captures Lambda execution logs for observability and debugging.

assumptions: Short codes are generated server-side as random alphanumeric strings (e.g. 7 characters) and collisions are retried.
Redirect uses an HTTP 302 response to the original URL.
No authentication is required; the API is publicly accessible.
Submitted URLs are validated for basic well-formedness before storage.
Visit count is incremented atomically using a DynamoDB update expression.
The stats endpoint returns 404 for unknown codes.

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 5 files — FastAPI URL shortener with a DynamoDB-backed storage layer decoupled behind a StorageRepository interface. Endpoints: POST /shorten (validates URL, generates unique short code with collision retry), GET /{code} (302 redirect + atomic visit increment), GET /stats/{code} (returns stats, 404 for unknown). AWS client reads AWS_ENDPOINT_URL and defaults region us-east-1; table name from URL_MAPPINGS_TABLE. Tests use an injected in-memory fake via dependency_overrides, run fully offline.

🏗️ Generated Terraform (initial): 4 files — Terraform for the url_shortener API mapped 1:1 to the plan's aws_resources: a DynamoDB table (url_mappings) with point-in-time recovery and KMS/CMK SSE; a Lambda function (url_shortener_fn) packaged inline via local_file + archive_file (no pre-built artifact), with reserved concurrency and KMS-encrypted env vars; an API Gateway v2 HTTP API (url_shortener_api) exposing POST /shorten, GET /{code}, GET /stats/{code} with access logging; a least-privilege IAM role (url_shortener_lambda_role) scoped to the specific table, log group and KMS key ARNs (no wildcards); and two KMS-encrypted CloudWatch log groups with retention. A dedicated KMS CMK (with rotation and a scoped key policy) backs encryption. The provider pins hashicorp/aws ~> 5.0 and sets default_tags (project, managed-by). Checks that are impossible on LocalStack Community or not applicable to this stateless architecture (Lambda VPC, DLQ, X-Ray, code signing) are handled with justified Checkov skip comments; all other AWS best-practice checks are satisfied natively.
